detail: read-only analysis of path_audit.py: what it checks, the core-vs-adapter scope tension, the gap against 7.3, and nine module defects nobody asked about

executed_by.mode: codex exec, one-shot, prompt on stdin, sandbox read-only
executed_by.delegated_internally: codex spawned its own subagents at gpt-5.6-terra medium, citing the repository's AGENTS.md

routing_finding.what: an interactive codex pane settled BLOCKED on a directory-trust modal for advanced-planning
routing_finding.handling: the pane was closed unanswered - a dialog is the operator's to clear - and the task rerouted to codex exec, which is non-interactive and has no trust gate
routing_finding.generalisation: the first-run trust dialog already recorded for cursor and claude applies to codex too. For read-only analysis codex exec sidesteps it entirely. Worth carrying into CLAUDE.md
routing_finding.proof_of_what_ran: the exec status line: model gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning effort high, sandbox read-only, approval never

the_finding_that_changes_the_plan.what: test_path_audit.py:237-252, TestFalsePositiveGuard::test_claude_skills_ref_is_not_flagged, writes a .claude/skills/ reference into core/agents/worker.md and asserts NO violation, calling it legitimate in its own name and docstring
the_finding_that_changes_the_plan.why_it_matters: that is exactly the behaviour 7.3 forbids and exactly what loop-003-2 exists to start failing. And it is not hypothetical - core/agents/worker.md is one of five real files under core/ carrying host tokens today
the_finding_that_changes_the_plan.consequence: loop-003-2's allowed_paths did not include the test file, which first becomes writable in 003-4, so the todo as written could not land a green suite
the_finding_that_changes_the_plan.resolution: dated amendment in phases/phase-6/plan.md - allowed_paths widened by one file, plus a check requiring the guard be INVERTED AND RENAMED, not deleted

the_gap_against_7_3.host_directories: partial, and only for .claude/, via two compound tokens. A bare .claude/, .cursor/, .opencode/, .codex/ is not a signature
the_gap_against_7_3.host_tool_names: not detectable - no pattern describes a tool or agent identifier
the_gap_against_7_3.host_permission_syntax: not detectable - no permission grammar is inspected
the_gap_against_7_3.core_as_a_whole: only core/agents and core/skills are scanned; core/schemas/ and core/state/ are outside every root, so the criterion is not enforced over all of core/
the_gap_against_7_3.correctly_marked_unverified_by_the_worke: the inventory of Claude-only tool names and the grammar of host permission syntax exist NOWHERE in the repository. 003-2 is defining that vocabulary, not implementing it

nine_module_defects_found_unprompted: _is_excluded does not match segments or prefixes despite its name - it is unanchored substring containment over the whole path, so a hypothetical core/skills/docs-writer/ is silently excluded by the 'docs' entry
the docstring's README*, CHANGELOG*, *.schema.md exclusions DO NOT EXIST anywhere in the module
and so those files ARE scanned - Path.suffix is the final suffix, so x.schema.md is .md
the suffix filter is an allowlist, not the binary-file check its comment claims; .py is silently skipped, so no Python file in a scanned root is ever audited
the docstring claims the doubled-prefix rule covers a backslash form the regex has no alternative for
the audit implements ONE of the five deprecated tokens docs/path-conventions.md:118-129 lists, and two of its three rules are not in that document at all

a missing scanned root is skipped silently and an OSError while reading returns 'no violations' - both turn absent coverage into a clean result, which is how the two absent .claude/ roots count as scanned today
the CI comment and the test helper both omit platforms/cowork from their copies of the root list - two independent transcriptions, wrong the same way
verification: every claim checked held: the test at 237-252, the absent README/CHANGELOG exclusion, the deprecated-token table, the suffix allowlist, the test helper's missing root, _is_excluded's substring semantics, the dead --verbose. Two of these were measured by the controller BEFORE dispatch precisely so the answer could be checked rather than believed; codex found both independently and eight more

detail: a core/-scoped host-neutrality rule in path_audit.py: three new patterns gated on the scanned root, the false-positive guard inverted and renamed rather than deleted, and the rule documented in path-conventions.md

dispatch_note.what: the first prompt pointed the worker at an envelope in the controller scratchpad and opencode settled BLOCKED on an 'Access external directory' permission dialog, so prompt --wait returned having collected nothing
dispatch_note.handling: the dialog was left for the operator, who cleared it; the durable fix for future dispatches is to deliver the envelope inline in the prompt, or inside the worktree, never by a path outside it
dispatch_note.generalisation: opencode gates directory access outside its worktree. Worth carrying into CLAUDE.md alongside the cursor and claude trust dialogs

the_defect_sent_back.what: category 2 was implemented as \b(Agent|Task|subagent_type)\b, which detects the English words Task and Agent
the_defect_sent_back.measured: 57 violations on the first commit, 37 from this rule, about 32 of those 37 being prose and markdown table headers - '| Loop | Task | Todos |', '## Task Decomposition Patterns', '# Agent Architecture', 'task_name:'
the_defect_sent_back.why_it_had_to_be_fixed_here: 003-3 is instructed to record the FULL first-run output as the finding. Shipping the noisy rule would have enshrined it and handed 003-4 a worklist saying to rewrite the word Task out of sentences
the_defect_sent_back.the_worker_named_it_itself: its reply listed the breadth of \bTask\b as ambiguity 2 and proposed a tighter form, then left it in - which is the envelope's 'name it, do not resolve it silently' working as intended
the_defect_sent_back.after: 36 violations, host-tool-name 37 -> 16, the other two rules untouched, every surviving hit naming a host. Pinned by a new test that plants the exact false-positive strings in a core/ fixture and requires a clean result

the_finding_that_corrects_my_own_record.what: 003-1's evidence, and 003-2's envelope repeating it, said the inventory of Claude-only tool names exists nowhere in the repository. It does
the_finding_that_corrects_my_own_record.where: example outcome: fields in the core skills' own reference docs - ralph-loop-planner/references/todo-schema.md:154 and :96, plan-todos/references/todo-schema.md:134 and :110
the_finding_that_corrects_my_own_record.significance: the project had written its own definition of a Claude-only name four times, as worked examples of a verifiable todo, and nobody had turned it into a check. The rule found its own specification by being run against real files - a rule written from the design paragraph alone would have kept the invented vocabulary
the_finding_that_corrects_my_own_record.deliberately_not_adopted: 'slash command' - an English phrase describing a concept rather than an identifier; matching it would have reintroduced the same false-positive class. Named rather than left implicit
the_finding_that_corrects_my_own_record.correction_recorded_in_place: a dated note now sits under the wrong paragraph in the 003-1 evidence file

the_inverted_guard: test_claude_skills_ref_is_not_flagged became test_claude_skills_ref_is_not_flagged_in_platforms with its content moved to platforms/claude-code/commands/install.md, and the old location and content - core/agents/worker.md carrying .claude/skills/ - reappear in a new TestHostNeutralityInCore class asserting the opposite. The legitimate case is preserved rather than lost, and the two tests now read side by side as the statement of the rule

named_decision_on_core_schemas_and_core_.answer: do not widen the scanned roots in this todo
named_decision_on_core_schemas_and_core_.worker_reason: the envelope scoped the work to a rule over already-scanned roots; widening surfaces hits in unreviewed files and is a larger change needing its own decision
named_decision_on_core_schemas_and_core_.controller_verdict: accepted - conservative and it keeps 003-3's finding bounded. But the success criterion is therefore met for core/agents/ and core/skills/ ONLY; core/schemas/ and core/state/ remain unenforced. Stated in three places now and still open; a candidate for its own todo, not a footnote

what_the_36_are.host-permission-syntax (9): almost entirely core/skills/permission-config/SKILL.md - a core skill whose whole subject is editing .claude/settings.json. Not a stray token: a Claude-only skill sitting in the platform-agnostic directory, and the largest thing the rule found
what_the_36_are.host-directory (11): hard-coded .claude/skills/, .claude/commands/ and ~/.claude/ lookup paths in skill-discovery instructions
what_the_36_are.host-tool-name (16): Claude Code named as the platform in core prose and a phase title
what_the_36_are.self_inflicted_class: five of the 36 are lines that FORBID the token and are flagged for containing it. A content-based suppression was deliberately refused - a rule that skips lines it recognises as prohibitions can be switched off by writing the right sentence, and this phase has already found four checks reporting green over ground they did not examine. 003-3 can reword five lines instead
